c.tagline: Albania's ancient port and its longest sun-soaked Adriatic beach.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing is limited, so taxis are the norm; agree a fare before setting off as meters are often not used, especially for the airport run to and from Tirana.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpocketing and bag-snatching on the crowded beach promenade and in summer nightlife areas, plus occasional taxi overcharging.

hood_desc: The compact historic core between the port and the Roman amphitheatre (the largest in the Balkans), with the Venetian Tower, Byzantine walls, museums, mosques, and churches; the sightseeing heart and most walkable base.
The long sandy beach strip and seafront promenade (Iliria) lined with hotels, cafes, seafood restaurants, and summer bars; the lively hub of Durrës's beach-holiday scene.
A quieter residential coastal area north of the center below King Zog's Villa hill, with small coves, calmer beaches, and a more local feel; good for a relaxed stay.
The cliffside 'Kavaja Rock' (Shkëmbi i Kavajës) stretch south of the city along the old Via Egnatia, a resort strip of beach hotels and clubs on the way toward Golem.
A major purpose-built beach-resort zone just south of Durrës proper, packed with large seaside hotels and resorts along a wide sandy shore; popular with families and summer package tourists.

water.note: Tap quality is inconsistent; stick to bottled water.

transit.hours: Local and intercity buses/furgons run roughly 05:00 to 20:00-21:00; there is no dedicated night service, so taxis fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Durrës has no metro or tram. Getting around relies on municipal buses, shared minibuses (furgons), taxis, and the compact, walkable historic center and beach promenade. Frequent furgons and a rail line link the city to Tirana.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (lek) directly to the driver or conductor on board (roughly 30-40 lek in town); there is no rechargeable transit card system.

bus: Intercity buses to other Albanian cities and international routes
ferry: Port of Durrës: car/passenger ferries to Bari and Ancona, Italy (Adria Ferries, GNV, Ventouris)
train: Hekurudha Shqiptare regional trains on the Durrës-Tirana line (limited service, undergoing redevelopment)

transit.m: Taxi/private transfer to Durrës city center (~35-45 min)
Airport bus to Tirana, then furgon or train onward to Durrës (~1.5-2 hr total)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.
